attackPath.severity_rationale: The off-by-one write is real but requires filling the table to capacity first, which is not demonstrated in the current main path. Impact is memory corruption but exploitability is lower than the buffer overflow.

attackPath.change_conditions: Severity would increase if the dangling pointer were written to. Setting to low if the freed memory is immediately reallocated in practice.
attackPath.dataflow: delete_record frees records[i].value -> lookup_record returns dangling pointer -> printf uses freed memory
attackPath.impact: Reading freed memory can leak stack/heap contents, cause undefined behavior, or crash the program. In a local CLI tool the impact is information disclosure or denial of service.
attackPath.reachability: Direct call sequence in main: the program adds a record, deletes it, then looks it up. The dangling pointer is read immediately.
attackPath.severity_rationale: The use-after-free is directly reachable in the default execution path and will read freed memory. However, the program only reads (not writes) the freed pointer, limiting impact to information disclosure or crash rather than code execution.

attackPath.dataflow: strdup returns NULL on allocation failure -> records[record_count].name/.value is NULL -> strcmp/free on NULL
attackPath.impact: NULL pointer dereference causes program crash (denial of service).
attackPath.reachability: Requires both external input driving add_record and system memory pressure causing strdup to fail. In normal local operation this is very unlikely.
attackPath.severity_rationale: NULL dereference is a crash but requires an unlikely combination of external input and memory pressure. Impact is limited to denial of service for a local CLI tool.
